![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/9c6353a4ab5578ffa3c05ca63d5d3d4887d276273016cc8b62ab66838a74286e.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<-0.73).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/4acdcc6571f10d5c7531510954bc245bcfd32cd0d281a5a380f0a9219a83694c.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>0.73).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/b0995edc5d1bc277c19d2a353b1cbae9a841dc8a04b30749a53db72153bdf2cb.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-0.73) & =P(Z>0.73) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.73) \\  & =1-Φ(0.73) \\  & =1-0.7673 \\  & =0.2327.\end{aligned}
$$
